title: Agent tool input still reaches the append-only audit log uncapped through approval previews and tool error strings
description: The new _logged_args cap (service.py:181-194) bounds only the two audit copies that pass through it (tool_request at 295-296, tool_execute at 413-414). The same agent-controlled strings still reach audit.append uncapped through two other sinks on the same request path. (1) For an approval-requiring call the payload appended at service.py:330-333 carries the preview dict verbatim (line 332); _preview returns sandbox.preview's preview_command, which copies the whole raw exec command (preview.py:131) and appends one note per command segment with no count cap (preview.py:125, only 'affected' is truncated at 126-128), and when _preview raises, the failure note embeds str(SandboxError) - that is the raw agent path from safe_path (service.py:319-320, sandbox.py:156). (2) For read_file, which the default policy allows without approval, the same SandboxError text is stored as tool_error payload.error (service.py:360-362). Neither the tool route (api.py:216; ToolCall.args is an unconstrained dict at api.py:51) nor the shipped reverse proxy (deploy/Caddyfile:5) bounds the body, and AuditLog.append inserts json.dumps(payload) with no size check (audit.py:183). Audit rows are append-only (audit.py:35-38), so every retained byte is permanent; at disk-full the audit-writing paths fail closed with 503.
root_cause: _call_tool caps only the two _logged_args mirrors (service.py:295-296, 413-414). The approval_requested payload passes preview through unchanged (service.py:330-333) while _preview copies the raw command and one note per segment (service.py:213-226, preview.py:125,131), and the SandboxError handler at service.py:360-362 logs str(e) untruncated although safe_path (sandbox.py:156) embeds the agent raw path. audit.append imposes no length bound of its own.
intended_behavior: Every payload that reaches the append-only audit log is bounded before the insert regardless of the producing call site: error strings, preview command, notes and affected paths are truncated to a fixed budget, the note count is capped, and the tool-args body is rejected above a small limit.

trace.description: Agent-token route; ToolCall.args (api.py:51-52) is parsed from the JSON body with no size limit, so the argument size equals what the agent sends.
Records args through the capped _logged_args, then evaluates policy; the capped copy is not the only path the arguments take.

For exec, sandbox.preview returns preview_command's full raw command; for an invalid workspace path, safe_path raises with the raw path and the handler at 319-320 turns str(e) into a preview note; raw args also go to ApprovalStore.create at 324.
The payload carries the preview dict minus the capture image with no truncation of command, notes or affected entries (line 332), written before any human is involved.
The untruncated str(e) is appended as payload.error; read_file and write_file need no approval, so this row is written on the first request.
json.dumps of the masked payload is inserted into the append-only audit table with no length or count bound.

evidence.description: The LOGGED_ARGS_MAX branch exists only inside _logged_args, whose two call sites are tool_request (295-296) and tool_execute (413-414); the preview/error sinks never pass through it.
approval_requested payload includes the preview dict verbatim.
A _preview failure is turned into a note containing the full exception text, i.e. the raw agent path from safe_path.
preview_command returns the full original command with no length cap.
One or more notes per command segment; the segment count is unbounded, only affected is truncated (126-128).
safe_path raises SandboxError with the raw agent path in the message.
SandboxError is a plain RuntimeError, so nothing shortens the message before it is logged as tool_error.
tool_error payload stores str(e) without truncation.
ToolCall.args is an unbounded dict; no route-level body limit exists.
Shipped proxy is a bare reverse_proxy with no request_body limit.
The DELETE trigger makes audit rows undeletable.
No size or count check on the inserted payload.
AuditWriteError is mapped to ServiceError 503, so the audit-log failure mode is fail-closed for every tool call.

conditions.description: Any valid agent token for one sandbox; the human token is not needed.
Default policy: delete_file always requires approval, non-allowlisted exec requires approval, while read_file and write_file are allowed, so the tool_error variant needs no approval at all.
None: approval_requested rows are written before any human sees the request, and the read_file variant needs no approval.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent sends one oversized tool argument and picks whichever tool gives the largest uncapped echo into the audit log.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/exec with a command of 2001 segments (10003 bytes)
instructions: In the approved OS-enforced sandbox (sbx v09: /target read-only on sys.path, /scratch writable, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 1 CPU, 120 s, no network, no Docker), run /scratch/v09_repro.py with /usr/bin/python3.

The script builds a real AgentBox with real AuditLog, ApprovalStore, Policy(default_policy.yaml), safe_path, SandboxManager.read_file and preview_command, faking only the Docker- and SQLite-facing SandboxManager methods (get, template_of, _require_running, _container, _expand, _walk, exists).
Call box.call_tool with each payload and read back SELECT id,actor,event,tool,length(payload) FROM audit plus length(args),length(preview) from the approvals table.
Attempt DELETE FROM audit on an oversized row, then set PRAGMA max_page_count as a deterministic full-disk stand-in and observe the next append and the following tool call.
execution.observed_result: tool_request stayed capped at 16,543 B in all three cases, but the other sinks did not: read_file with a 131,072-byte path outside /workspace returned 400 with a 131,115-byte message and wrote a 131,142-byte tool_error row with no approval; delete_file with a 262,144-byte path wrote a 262,342-byte approval_requested row whose single preview note began '미리보기 실패: 허용되지 않은 경로: /etc/AAAA…' (approval row: 262,156 B args, 262,244 B preview); exec with a 10,003-byte, 2001-segment command wrote a 96,207-byte approval_requested row carrying the full 10,003-byte preview.command and 2,001 notes (approval row: 10,018 B args, 96,109 B preview). DELETE FROM audit raised 'audit log is append-only'. With the page cap as a full-disk stand-in the append raised AuditWriteError 'database or disk is full' and the following tool call failed closed with 503.

remediation.strategy: Bound payloads at the sink and at the producers: one recursive bounder inside AuditLog.append (string truncation plus list/dict cap) applied before compute_hash so verify() stays consistent, truncate the preview command/notes/affected and the SandboxError text before they are appended, and reject oversized tool-args bodies at the route with a request_body limit in the shipped proxy as defense in depth.

code_changes.fixed_code:
AUDIT_TEXT_MAX = 512

def _audit_text(s: Any) -> str:
    t = str(s)
    return t if len(t) <= AUDIT_TEXT_MAX else t[:AUDIT_TEXT_MAX] + f"...({len(t)} bytes)"

# _preview failure note and exec command, before they are appended/created:
notes = [f"미리보기 실패: {_audit_text(e)}"]
preview["command"] = _audit_text(preview.get("command"))
preview["notes"] = [_audit_text(n) for n in (preview.get("notes") or [])][:200]
preview["affected"] = (preview.get("affected") or [])[:200]

# SandboxError handler:
except SandboxError as e:
    short = _audit_text(e)
    self.log_best_effort(sid, tool, "tool_error", {"request": req_id, "error": short})
    raise ServiceError(400, short) from e

likelihood.reason: One authenticated agent request per row; the read_file variant needs no approval, snapshot or concurrency, and the row size follows the request body size.

impact.reason: Permanent undeletable growth of the shared control-plane SQLite file; at disk-full the tool, approval and lifecycle paths fail closed with 503 and recovery needs an operator to rebuild the database and rebuild the hash chain. Not RCE or a guaranteed crash.

confidence.reason: Every cited line was re-read in the audited tree (9805d91) and the minimum observed result was independently reproduced: 131,142 B and 262,342 B and 96,207 B rows against a 16,543 B capped tool_request, a real append-only DELETE rejection, and a fail-closed 503 after a page-capped append, with only the Docker-facing SandboxManager faked.
